title.es: When y while: dos acciones en el pasado

objective: Al terminar cuentas una acción interrumpida (pasado continuo + pasado simple) con when y while.

warmup.prompt_es: 'Estaba caminando cuando vi un accidente.' ¿Qué acción es larga, cuál es corta y qué palabra las une?

input.text: Yesterday I was cycling to work when it started to rain. While I was looking for shelter, my phone rang. It was my boss. She was waiting for me in a meeting, but I was stuck in the rain! In the end, I arrived late while everybody was having coffee.
input.es: Ayer iba en bicicleta al trabajo cuando empezó a llover. Mientras buscaba refugio, sonó mi teléfono. Era mi jefa. Me estaba esperando en una reunión, ¡pero yo estaba atrapado bajo la lluvia! Al final, llegué tarde mientras todos tomaban café.

glossary.example: I was stuck in the rain.
In the end, I arrived late.
While I was walking, I saw a dog.
I was walking when I saw a dog.

md_es: *I was cycling **when** it started to rain.* · *While I was looking for shelter, my phone **rang**.*
- **Dos acciones largas a la vez:** *While I was reading, my brother **was watching** TV.*
- **Dos acciones cortas una tras otra:** pasado simple + pasado simple: *When I arrived, she left.*
| **when** | la acción corta (pasado simple) | *…when it started to rain.* |
| **while** | la acción larga (pasado continuo) | *While I was looking…* |
**Puntuación:** si la frase empieza con *when / while*, lleva coma: *While I was walking, I saw an accident.* Si no, sin coma: *I saw an accident while I was walking.*
**Ojo:** *while* + pasado continuo; no se usa con verbos de estado (*while I knew*). Para 'mientras' = *while*, no *when*.

common_mistakes_es.wrong: I was cooking when the phone was ringing.
common_mistakes_es.right: I was cooking when the phone rang.
common_mistakes_es.note: La interrupción es una acción corta.

common_mistakes_es.wrong: When I was cooking, he was watching TV.
common_mistakes_es.right: While I was cooking, he was watching TV.
